question: What is the training target of a plain autoencoder?
options: The class label of the input
The input itself
A random noise vector
The next example in the dataset
explanation: An autoencoder is trained to reconstruct its own input, so no labels are needed.

question: What stops an autoencoder from simply learning the identity function?
options: The sigmoid on the output
Using Adam instead of SGD
A code (bottleneck) much smaller than the input
Shuffling the training data
explanation: With a 2- or 8-number code the network cannot pass every pixel through, so it must keep only the factors that explain most of the data.

question: An autoencoder with no activation functions, trained with squared error, converges to which solution?
options: The same subspace as PCA with the same reconstruction error
A perfect reconstruction of every image
A random projection
The same solution as k-means
explanation: The best rank-k linear reconstruction under squared error is the top-k principal subspace; the script shows 0.0529 for both at code size 2.

question: Why does the nonlinear autoencoder beat PCA at the same code size?
options: It uses more training data
It can map a curved data manifold into the code, while PCA only projects onto a flat subspace
It uses labels during training
PCA is computed incorrectly on images
explanation: Real images lie near curved surfaces; nonlinear encoders and decoders can unroll and re-roll them.

question: You decode a random point from the 2D code space of a plain autoencoder and get a blurry mess. Why?
options: The decoder has a bug
Plain autoencoders do not constrain the code space, so random points can fall in regions no training image maps to
2D codes can never be decoded
The sigmoid saturates for all codes
explanation: Nothing forces the codes to fill a known region; that is what the variational autoencoder adds.

question: The 2D code gives 0.71 nearest-centroid accuracy (chance is 0.10) without using labels in training. What does that show?
options: The autoencoder secretly saw the labels
The test set is too small to measure anything
Any random 2D projection of pixels gets the same score
Reconstruction alone pushed similar digits to similar codes, so the code captures class structure
explanation: Similar images need similar codes to be rebuilt similarly, so class structure emerges in the code even though labels were only used afterwards to measure it.
